m.com/cli/reference.md).\n## Cloud credentials and API URL\n`--api-key` and `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud` and work be
fore or after descendants (`mcpjam cloud --api-key sk_… eval list` and `mcpjam cloud eval list --api-key sk_…` are the same). Loca
l commands, including hosted `readiness`, reject those flags at the program root. Hosted `readiness` still takes leaf `--api-key`.

Credential precedence for Cloud commands:
1. `--api-key`: must be an `sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.
2. `
MCPJAM_API_KEY`: same `sk_` rule. A legacy value in this env var is ignored (with a warning) so SDK eval reporting can still use i
t.\n3. Stored OAuth from `mcpjam cloud login`\n4. Missing: Cloud commands fail with login guidance before they hit the network (`m
cpjam cloud status` reports `missing` instead)\n3. The server saved with the OAuth login (only when that login is the credential;
a login saved before logins recorded their server counts as MCPJam Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address is
refused with exit `3`)\nEvery command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its server
when it starts, before it contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `http(s
)` URL, or that carries credentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming diffe
rent servers. The error masks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login is
only sent to its own server: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3` before any reque
st. `mcpjam cloud status` uses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false`,
includes `credential.valid` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (`cr
edential.valid: null`) and successful.\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud as … · pro
ject: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.\n## Cloud p

# Local Evals

> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine
with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity\n\n`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects
your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, a
nd decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your own provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-hos
ted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.\n\nResults are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to your t
erminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the run start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single ano
nymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.md) event, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off; the run

adds no telemetry of its own.

## Eval identity and local data

Run `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` to a
n organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK also accepts `apiKey` or `mcpjamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take precedence
over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, which takes precedence over the saved CLI login. An invalid explicit credential never falls back to anothe
r account. CI never starts an interactive login. Ask an organization admin for a key if you cannot create one.\n\nEvery logical ru
n needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transient failures within ten seconds, then stops before execution. A prior succe
ssful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI resolves the project using its existing `--project`, environment, and linked-
project settings; a key can only access its own organization.\n\nWith results uploads disabled, the start-run request sends only t
he credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API headers you configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam`, proje
ct selection, a new run-start ID, client version and surface (SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider names, and w
hether a client profile is used (`unknown` for custom executors). The server resolves the organization and account. The start-run
request sends no prompts, outputs, tool calls, or server URLs. MCPJam-hosted inference still sends prompts through MCPJam to the m
odel, as before. Retries reuse the same ID. Planned iterations are intent, not completed usage or a charge. This release adds no d
ebit, quota draw, or balance refusal.\n\n`DO_NOT_TRACK`, `MCPJAM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, and CLI telemetry settings disable analytics

, not the required run-start request. Results remain local unless result uploading is enabled separately.
